newsitem.title: GERMANY: Post-EMU bond mkt seen much smaller than U.S. - bank.
newsitem.headline: Post-EMU bond mkt seen much smaller than U.S. - bank.

text.p: The European bond market will be roughly about the size of Japan's and considerably smaller than the U.S. market after the planned launch of the single currency, the euro, in January 1999, BHF-Bank said in a research report.

Basing its calculations on Bank for International Settlements data, BHF said the domestic markets of all EU states taken together accounted for bonds outstanding worth about 7.5 trillion dollars in 1996.
That compares with about 11 trillion dollars for the U.S. and about five trillion dollars in Japan.
But BHF said the odds are small that all EU nations will intially join European monetary union and a euro bond market consisting of a "core" group of nations would amount to about four billion marks.
If Italy, Spain and Portugal were to join the single currency project in 1999, the new market for euro-denominated debt would be about 6.25 trillion dollars.
Once the single European currency is launched, member nations are obliged to issue debt denominated in euros and are expected to convert existing debt into the single European currency.
